population.note: FICTIONAL. All incretin use, any reason. About 15% of ~265M US adults (~39.8M) are currently on a drug; 21% (~55.7M) have ever used one; 6% (~15.9M) used and are off now. Cycling arithmetic: about 40% of current users have restarted at least once (6.0 pts), plus about a quarter of the off-now group cycled before stopping again (1.5 pts), giving 7.5/21 ≈ 36% of ever-users. That fits the parent's ~1/3 one-year persistence and 36–47% restart rate. Age bands, weighted by adult population shares (20/33/24/23%), give ~15.0%. The 65+ band rose from 9% to 12% because of the Medicare $0 generic programme, despite the bone/muscle warnings. Payer split of the ~39.8M current users: ~11M public (Medicare ~6.0M, Medicaid ~5.0M), ~15M employer/commercial, ~11.3M cash, ~2.5M gray market only. The income gap has narrowed but not closed. At $49–69/month cash the generic is affordable to most people, but the $0 public route requires a smartphone-paired scale, monthly weigh-ins and ≥80% refill adherence. About 18% of programme enrollees lost $0 status at their first six-month check; most moved to cash generic, stopped, or went to the gray market. Never-users with obesity in the bottom third live disproportionately in the ~26 states not in the Medicaid model. Pediatric: 0.9% of under-18s, mostly adolescents 12–17 on generic semaglutide. Roughly a quarter of US children now live with at least one adult on an incretin.

access.public_coverage: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot expired Dec 2027 as scheduled. It was replaced from Jan 2028 by a CMMI 'Metabolic Health Access' model. Generic semaglutide is $0 to Medicare Part D enrollees and to Medicaid enrollees in 24 participating states who meet BMI ≥30 (or ≥27 with comorbidity) criteria. Continued $0 status requires ≥80% refill adherence (pharmacy data), monthly weigh-ins on a programme-issued cellular scale and ≥5% loss at 6 months, plus an annual DEXA and chair-stand test for those 65+. Branded drugs (tirzepatide, oral Wegovy, Foundayo) stay at the Nov 2025 deal rate of ~$245/month with a $50 copay, under step therapy. Spending arithmetic (annualised, Dec 2028): ~4.5M on $0 generic × $42/month net incl. dispensing × 12 = ~$2.3B; ~6.5M on branded at $245 × 12 = ~$19.1B; total ~$21.4B/yr across Medicare and Medicaid for ~11M users. Generic substitution is pulling the branded share down quarter by quarter.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India 60+ brands at $6–40/month; Canada generics ~CAD 70–110 and the source for Florida's state importation programme; Brazil, Mexico and much of the Gulf supplied by Indian makers; generic semaglutide in ~160 countries as forecast.
access.note: Generic collapse runs on one molecule only. After Novo's Nov 2027 patent settlement, licensed generic and authorised-generic injectable semaglutide reached US pharmacies from Apr 2028. Cash prices: $49–69/month at warehouse clubs and cost-plus pharmacies by Q3. Oral Wegovy and Foundayo cash fell to $99–149. Tirzepatide has no generic: $349–499 cash via LillyDirect. Retatrutide (approved Apr 2028) lists at $1,199 and is rarely covered. Employer coverage recovered from 60% to 64%, almost entirely generic-first. ~55% of covering employers route anything branded through PBM 'metabolic management' programmes with connected-scale weigh-ins and loss targets. ~30% tie a premium differential ($20–50/month) to wellness-programme participation. The gray market regrew after the 503B exclusion was finalised (Jun 2027). It sells 'research-use' tirzepatide, retatrutide ('reta') and cagrilintide from Chinese and Indian synthesisers at $90–180/month via offshore telehealth and Telegram/Discord vendors. Its customers are people priced out of branded tirzepatide, people who fail coverage conditions, and people who don't want to be tracked. Route: weekly injectables still slightly ahead by volume because the cheapest product is the generic pen, but orals are ~55% of new starts.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic; US generic and authorised generic from Apr 2028)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro; brand only)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 small-molecule, daily oral (orforglipron: Foundayo, high-dose label added 2027)
GLP-1 + amylin combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema, approved Jan 2027)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, approved Apr 2028)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: alcohol reduction: phase 3 programmes ongoing, still no approval; widely prescribed off-label by addiction clinics
microdosing / 'metabolic health' use by non-obese adults, now cheap via generic semaglutide
scheduled 'drug holidays' and dose-down around occasions, discussed openly by prescribers
pediatric under-12 use off-label under specialist care
gray-market retatrutide and cagrilintide stacking by gym and biohacker communities
drugs.pipeline_note: No new indication was approved this step. CagriSema was approved Jan 2027 from its pending NDA. Uptake is modest because it failed non-inferiority against tirzepatide. Retatrutide's BLA was filed Mar 2027 and approved Apr 2028, 13 months later, after a review extended over the dysesthesia signal. Its label is limited to BMI ≥35, or ≥30 with comorbidity, and carries lean-mass language. Oral parity was realised through an existing product in a new form, not a new molecule. A 2027 head-to-head trial showed high-dose orforglipron non-inferior to injectable semaglutide 2.4 mg (~15% vs ~15% at 72 weeks), and FDA added the higher dose. No pill yet matches tirzepatide or retatrutide. Amycretin is in phase 3, survodutide filing expected 2029, and MariTide is in phase 3; none is on the US market. Bimagrumab and other muscle-preserving adjuncts are in phase 2 and also sold gray-market.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Repeated on/off cycling re-exposes users to escalation-phase GI effects.
Elevated with rapid weight loss, more visible with retatrutide's larger losses.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Gray-market product reports muddy the signal.

Recognised as a population problem. Claims and DEXA-registry data show clinically meaningful sarcopenia (grip strength and gait speed falls) concentrated in users 65+ and in users on continuous therapy beyond 2 years. Losses compound in people who cycle, because weight regained off-drug is disproportionately fat.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA class labelling update (Jul 2028): resistance training and ≥1.2 g/kg protein, baseline and annual DEXA for 65+. CMS programme conditions $0 status for 65+ on an annual DEXA/chair-stand test. Retatrutide label carries lean-mass language.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fractures
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New entry. Large Medicare and VA cohort analyses (2028) find hip BMD losses of ~2–3% over two years and roughly 25–35% higher fragility-fracture rates in users 65+ on therapy beyond two years, compared with matched non-users. Signal is weaker under 50. Earlier gout and osteomalacia reports remain unresolved.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Bone-health warning added in the Jul 2028 class labelling update; ASBMR/Endocrine Society joint guidance. No restriction on use.
EMA 'very rare' label stands; no US class label.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Now a mainstream complaint. Fictional 2027–28 surveys put self-reported 'flattening at least sometimes' at ~20–25% of current users, and ~29% deliberately skip doses for occasions. Still no trial designed to measure it. Dose reduction is the standard first response.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA requested postmarketing patient-reported-outcome studies for retatrutide and Foundayo; no label language.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Real-world regain sits between trial and claims estimates. Programme-driven stops (failed adherence checks) produce a visible regain cohort.
Overlaps with the protein and bone story; vitamin D and B12 testing increasingly routine.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Referenced in the 2028 class guidance; no label change.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; effects in adolescents who may take these for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Roughly six years of rigorous follow-up now exists. The bone finding is the first long-horizon effect to firm up. Adolescent bone accrual is the open question.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements continue; NIH adolescent bone-accrual cohort funded 2028.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / gray-market product harms (dosing errors, contamination, unapproved molecules)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Adverse-event reports rose again after mid-2027 and now include pre-approval retatrutide, mislabelled vials and peptide stacks.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 503B exclusion finalised Jun 2027; import alerts and warning letters; enforcement struggles against offshore 'research-use' sellers.

food_and_beverage.state: Generic prices took the drug down-market. Adoption in lower-income households is now hitting categories the affluent wave barely touched: value soda, dollar-store snacks, frozen meals. Salty-snack and confectionery US volumes are falling ~3–4% a year, and GLP-1 households are ~30% of households. Protein fortification is near-universal. The aesthetic inversion gives 'muscle' positioning (whey, high-protein dairy, jerky) a second wind.

alcohol.state: Spirits and beer volumes keep declining. Addiction clinics prescribe off-label. Drug holidays create a spiky pattern: users skip a dose before weddings and holidays and drink in bursts, which on-premise operators now plan promotions around.

restaurants.state: Traffic holds and check sizes stay flat. Half portions and 'tasting' formats are standard. In Manhattan and Los Angeles the inversion has revived conspicuous appetite: steakhouses, whole-fish service and 'eat everything' tasting menus as a status display by people who signal they are off the drug.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking store counts. Mainstream brands adapt with stretch sizing for cyclers whose weight swings. Athletic brands sell 'built' fits cut for shoulders and glutes rather than smallness.

fitness.state: The muscle and bone wave plus the new body ideal make strength the growth category. DEXA scan chains, physical-therapy-led 'muscle clinics' for over-60s and resistance-training studios are expanding. Medicare's DEXA condition sends a steady stream of older users to body-composition providers.

insurance.state: Generic step therapy cut GLP-1 cost per member sharply, and employers re-added coverage (60%→64%). They attached conditions instead: PBM metabolic programmes, connected-scale monitoring, loss targets and premium differentials. The pharmacy-trend debate shifted from GLP-1s to retatrutide and to fracture and physical-therapy downstream costs.

pharma.state: Lilly dominates: tirzepatide, high-dose Foundayo, retatrutide. Novo is restructuring around CagriSema and orals after giving up the US injectable semaglutide franchise to generics. Viatris and Teva are the generic semaglutide volume players. US revenue per patient is falling while patient counts rise, and the gray market takes share at the premium end.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thinness no longer reads as discipline or wealth. It reads as a $49 pen or a Medicaid scale. Visible muscle, a big appetite and claimed 'unmedicated vitality' are the new scarce signals, because they take time, trainers, protein and good genes.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The class gradient flipped in signalling but not in health. Thin is cheap. Muscle is expensive: coaching, DEXA, a protein budget and free hours. Among college-educated women 25–39 in Los Angeles, Austin and Brooklyn, 'natty' (never-medicated or off-drug) is a stated identity on dating profiles and in gym marketing. Lower-income users are thinner than their parents and are told by a new ideal that thin is not enough.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Two cultures share one table. Medicated households eat small, and have their main meal around the weekly dose. Off-drug affluent circles stage abundance, finishing the plate as performance. Thanksgiving and weddings are now 'skip-week' occasions, planned around a missed dose.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: 'On or off?' is an ordinary early-date question. Couples coordinate drug holidays for anniversaries and trips. 'Flat' is common shorthand for a partner who seems emotionally absent on-drug. Some advertise 'off-drug' as a sign of sensuality.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite has been revalued. Medicine treats it as a symptom; the culture now treats it as a sign of being alive. Hunger, eating a lot and wanting things are marketed as vitality by brands, gyms and restaurants that serve people who can afford to want.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: Fictional 2027–28 survey estimates: ~20–25% of current users report flattening at least sometimes, and ~29% deliberately skip doses for occasions or 'to feel things'. Clinicians routinely offer dose-down or a holiday. Unmeasured in trials. The $0 public programme's ≥80% adherence rule limits how many holidays enrollees can take.
interior_life.framing: Mostly a side effect, and increasingly a lifestyle management problem, like caffeine tolerance. Addiction medicine frames the same effect as treatment, and some users call it relief ('the noise is gone'). The new body ideal calls it a loss of character.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Mixed and anecdotal-plus-survey. Some sales and hospitality managers report on-drug staff as steadier but less driven. Users in repetitive jobs often report the quiet as useful. Holidays are scheduled around pitches and performances. No employer encourages the drug for performance; some coaches warn creatives off high doses.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Musicians and comedians talk publicly about dosing down before tours. 'Skip-week' parties are a recognised social form. Sour, spicy and extreme-flavour products and loud, high-intensity entertainment hold a niche among on-drug consumers chasing a signal.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Reduced desire is a widely acknowledged complaint. Couples therapists ask about dosing schedules. Drug holidays around anniversaries are common advice.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The complaint has become a talking point. Populist health-skeptic voices frame cheap provision as 'pharma sedating the country' while the administration takes credit for the $49 price, so the right is split. Disability and fat-acceptance groups oppose the adherence conditions as surveillance. No measurable effect on turnout or partisanship.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access on price and approvals: the settlement was encouraged, retatrutide was approved, the oral high-dose label was added. Pro-crackdown on compounding, but losing ground to offshore 'research-use' sellers. Added a bone and muscle class warning without restricting use.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Direct subsidy. $0 generic semaglutide for eligible Medicare and Medicaid (24 states) enrollees under a CMMI model, ~$2.3B/yr for ~4.5M people. Branded drugs stay at $245/$50. No mandate to take the drug.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The $0 public route is conditioned on refill adherence, monthly cellular-scale weigh-ins, a ≥5% loss at 6 months and annual DEXA/strength testing for 65+. Employer and PBM programmes use similar weigh-in data, and ~30% of covering employers tie premium differentials to participation. Privacy advocates and some state attorneys general are challenging the sharing of weight data with plan sponsors.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE covers generic semaglutide for dependents and retirees. The services allow on-drug active-duty members who pass strength-based fitness tests, and several installations are trialling DEXA in place of tape tests. No workforce mandate.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Generic semaglutide API comes largely from Indian makers, and Florida imports Canadian generics under its state programme. Gray-market tirzepatide and retatrutide peptides come mostly from Chinese synthesisers, so peptide supply is now part of US–China trade and customs talks. The US–India price gap has narrowed from ~30× to ~3×.

events.event: FDA finalises exclusion of semaglutide, tirzepatide and liraglutide from the 503B bulks list; within months offshore telehealth and 'research-use' vendors are selling tirzepatide and pre-approval retatrutide at $90–180 a month, and import alerts fail to stem the flow
Head-to-head trial finds high-dose orforglipron (Foundayo) non-inferior to weekly injectable semaglutide 2.4 mg at ~15% weight loss; FDA adds the higher dose to the label in December

Novo Nordisk settles US semaglutide patent litigation with Viatris and other generic filers, licensing entry from April 2028 and launching its own authorised generic; Florida's Canadian importation programme and federal price pressure cited; cash prices reach $49–69 a month by Q3 2028

Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot ends and CMS launches a CMMI model giving $0 generic semaglutide to eligible Medicare and Medicaid enrollees in 24 states, conditioned on refill adherence, monthly cellular-scale weigh-ins and 5% loss at six months

After Medicare and VA cohorts show elevated fragility fractures and hip bone loss in users 65+ on therapy beyond two years, FDA adds a class bone and muscle warning recommending baseline DEXA and resistance training
National poll: 15% of US adults currently on an incretin drug; 29% of users say they deliberately skip doses for social occasions or 'to feel things'

open_tensions: The $0 public programme demands ≥80% adherence, yet drug holidays are the standard remedy for flattening. Enrollees must choose between feeling things and keeping free coverage, and failed checks are pushing people into a cash or gray-market cycle.

The subsidy is raising adoption among people 65+ just as the bone and muscle warning lands. Nobody has settled whether fracture and physical-therapy costs offset the cardiometabolic savings, or who pays for the DEXA and strength infrastructure.

Only semaglutide got cheap. Tirzepatide and retatrutide are brand-priced and rarely covered, so the efficacy frontier is supplied increasingly by an unregulated peptide market with no long-horizon data.
Thinness has become a commodity and muscle a class marker. Adolescents on decades-long therapy face a body ideal their drug works against, while their bone accrual is unmeasured.
still_true: Tirzepatide (Zepbound/Mounjaro) has no US generic; Lilly sells it brand-only, including through LillyDirect.
Medicare pays ~$245/month for branded GLP-1s with a ~$50 beneficiary copay under the Nov 2025 Lilly/Novo deal terms.
Alcohol reduction remains off-label: no GLP-1 is approved for alcohol use disorder.
The FDA's Jan 2026 removal of the suicidal-ideation warning stands; the effect remains classed as debunked.
India's patent-lapsed generic semaglutide market keeps dozens of brands selling for under $50 a month.

prose.headline: Thin Is Free Now. Muscle Is the New Money: Inside America's $49 Pen, Its Weigh-In Scales and the Body Nobody Can Buy
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2028, about one American adult in seven is on an incretin drug, and about one in five has tried one. The most consequential change of the past two years is the price, not a molecule. In November 2027 Novo Nordisk settled its patent fight with the generic makers rather than wait out its exclusivity while Florida imported Canadian generics and Washington leaned on it. By the following summer, generic semaglutide pens sat on warehouse-club pharmacy shelves for $49 to $69 a month. The pill caught up at almost the same moment. A head-to-head trial showed high-dose Foundayo doing what the weekly shot does, and over half of new patients now never touch a needle.

Cheap did not mean free of conditions. When the Medicare bridge pilot expired, CMS replaced it with a model that gives generic semaglutide away at no cost to eligible Medicare enrollees and Medicaid enrollees in two dozen states. It costs about two billion dollars a year. Every enrollee also gets a grey cellular scale that reports to the plan each month. Miss a fifth of your refills, or fail to lose five percent in six months, and the free drug becomes a $49 drug. Nearly a fifth of the first cohort failed the six-month check. Employers who had dropped coverage came back, because generics made it cheap. They came back with weigh-ins, loss targets and premium differentials attached. The arguments now are about who sees the numbers on the scale.

The drugs that actually lead on efficacy stayed expensive. Tirzepatide has no generic. Retatrutide was approved in April at nearly $1,200 a month, with a narrow label and lean-mass language, and almost nobody's plan pays for it. People who couldn't get it legally had already found it. After the FDA finally shut compounders out, the trade moved offshore into 'research-use' vials of tirzepatide, retatrutide and amylin analogues, shipped from Chinese synthesisers and dosed from Discord spreadsheets. Two and a half million Americans use nothing else.

In July the agency added the warning the orthopaedists had been predicting. Medicare and VA data showed hip bone loss and a clear rise in fragility fractures among users over 65 who had stayed on the drug more than two years. Now the label recommends a DEXA scan and resistance training, and the free programme requires an annual scan and a chair-stand test for older enrollees. Body-composition clinics have opened in strip malls. Physical therapists have waiting lists.

The culture got there first. When thinness cost a thousand dollars a month it meant money. Now it costs a Medicaid card, and in the affluent neighbourhoods of Los Angeles, Austin and Brooklyn the prized body is a muscled one with a visible appetite. 'Natty' appears on dating profiles. Steakhouses are full of people finishing the plate as a performance. Apparel brands cut for shoulders. Food companies still lose volume, faster now that the drug has reached the dollar-store customer, and they sell protein to everyone.

On the drug, the complaint everyone recognises is flatness. A quarter of users say they feel it at least sometimes. Nearly a third skip doses before weddings, tours, anniversaries and Thanksgiving, and doctors help them plan it. 'Skip week' is an ordinary phrase. The people with the least room to skip are those on the free programme, whose adherence is counted. Nothing has collapsed. Obesity keeps falling. The country looks healthier from a distance, and it is also weighed, scanned and somewhat quieter.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Ray Delgado steps on the grey scale at 6:10 because the app on his phone chimes at 6:10. 211.4. The little green check appears and the screen says GOOD MORNING, RAYMOND, ON TRACK. He was 262 when he started.

The pen is in the butter drawer of the fridge, next to the insulin he no longer needs. Thursday. He does it in the thigh, standing, the way the pharmacist at the Tucson Costco showed him. Medicare pays for the generic now. It costs him nothing.

At ten he has the scan. The technician is a kid with forearms like hams and a T-shirt that says BUILT NOT BOUGHT. Ray lies still while the arm passes over him. The kid shows him a colour picture of his own hip, purple and green, and a number lower than last year's. 'Bands,' the kid says. 'Every day. And eggs.' He hands Ray a printout and a coupon for whey.

After lunch, a half sandwich, he does the bands in the carport while the radio plays a song he used to love. He waits for the song to do something.

At four his granddaughter Marisol calls about the quinceañera. Two Saturdays from now. 'Abuelo, skip that week. Please. I want you to dance. I want you to eat the cake.'

He looks at the calendar. If he skips a refill he drops below eighty. He did the math once with his son-in-law on a napkin.

'We'll see, mija,' he says.

He writes CAKE in pencil on the Saturday, then puts the pencil down and goes out to the carport to do another set.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot ends and CMS launches a CMMI model giving $0 generic semaglutide to eligible Medicare and Medicaid enrollees in 24 states
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the model starts in Jan 2028 and hands out $0 generic semaglutide, but generics only reach US pharmacies in Apr 2028. The 18% six-month-check failures and 4.5M generic enrollees by Dec 2028 are squeezed into the months after launch.

Mechanism and magnitude: the world says generic substitution and step therapy dominate, yet 6.5M public users (59%) stay on branded drugs at Dec 2028, only nine months after generics arrive. The prose then says the programme 'costs about two billion dollars a year', ignoring the $19B branded line.

Magnitude: 0.9% of all under-18s is about 650k children. The parent had only ~0.6% of children with obesity on the drug, which is roughly 0.1% of all children, so this is a many-fold jump in two years with no pediatric driver or mechanism.

rationale.badness: The world is recognisably harder. Free coverage is conditioned on cellular-scale weigh-ins and ≥80% refill adherence, and about 18% of enrollees lose $0 status at the first check. 65+ users face fracture and sarcopenia risk, 20–25% report flattening, and the offshore gray market has 2.5M exclusive users. Offsets are cheap access, falling obesity, and a flattened thinness gradient, so inequality is mixed. Harms are mostly named and measured, so the epistemic score stays moderate. Overall is a middle-to-hard 5.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visible in fields and events: 15% adoption, a settlement-driven generic collapse, adherence conditioning, the bone/muscle warning, orforglipron parity, gray-market regrowth, the 'natty' inversion, the $0 subsidy, and mainstream flattening. Approvals follow the envelope (CagriSema Jan 2027, retatrutide 13 months after filing). mechanism: causal chains are mostly shown, but the $0 generic model starts in Jan 2028 before generics exist (claim 1), and branded drugs dominate public volume despite generic-first step therapy (claim 2). The flip of the culture toward muscle is partly asserted. magnitude: 15% current and 21% ever are inside the envelope, and the cycling, age-band, payer-split and $2.3B/$19.1B arithmetic all reconcile. Deductions are for the pediatric 0.9% jump (claim 3) and the prose '$2B a year' that contradicts the $21.4B total.
rationale.generativity: The Ray Delgado scene is concrete: the 6:10 scale chime, the butter-drawer pen, the DEXA tech in a BUILT NOT BOUGHT shirt, the unmoved song, and the CAKE pencil mark against the 80% refill threshold. The world also implies many more scenes: skip-week parties, 'natty' dating profiles, PBM weigh-in disputes, and gray-market Discord vendors.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot ends and CMS launches a CMMI model giving $0 generic semaglutide to eligible Medicare and Medicaid enrollees in 24 states, conditioned on refill adherence, monthly cellular-scale weigh-ins and 5% loss at six months
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the $0 generic model starts in Jan 2028, but the world says licensed generics only reached US pharmacies from Apr 2028. The 6-month check on which 18% lost status would then have fallen at or before generic launch, so the timeline contradicts itself.

Magnitude/mechanism: the same field says branded drugs sit under step therapy and generic is $0, yet 59% of public users (6.5M of 11M) are on $245 branded product. That is hard to square with generic substitution, and it makes the public bill about 9× the generic line.

least_plausible_claims.quote: roughly 25–35% higher fragility-fracture rates in users 65+ on therapy beyond two years, compared with matched non-users
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude/mechanism: a firm, large fracture signal in a 2028 Medicare/VA cohort with more than two years of therapy is fast, since Medicare obesity coverage began only in mid-2026. It is also observational and confounded, yet it is treated as 'established' within the window.

rationale.badness: The world is harder but not collapsed. A $0 public route is conditioned on cellular-scale weigh-ins and 80% adherence, which pushes people toward cash or gray-market cycling. Flattening is reported by 20–25% of users, there is a bone and fracture signal in the 65+ group, and a gray market of unregulated peptides. Thinness is cheap but a new muscle-based class marker has emerged, and adolescents on long-term therapy have unmeasured bone accrual. The harms are named and measured, so epistemic badness is moderate, and there is no melodrama.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is traceable to fields and events. The adoption delta lands at 15%, generic collapse comes via the Nov 2027 settlement, and conditioning and subsidy appear in the CMMI model. The bone/muscle wave, oral parity (high-dose Foundayo), gray-market resurgence, aesthetic inversion and the mainstream complaint are all shown. new_indications is empty and the retatrutide and CagriSema approvals respect the approval rules. mechanism: most chains are shown (settlement → $49 pens → down-market F&B; 503B exclusion → gray market; adherence rule → holiday conflict). The Jan 2028 $0 generic precedes the Apr 2028 generic launch (claim 1), and the branded-heavy public mix conflicts with step therapy (claim 2). The 2028 fracture finding is fast (claim 3). magnitude: population figures sit inside the envelope, with 15% on drug and 21% ever. The age-band weighting gives about 15.0, the income gradient brackets the national figure, the payer split sums to 39.8M, and the cycling arithmetic gives 36%. Spending of $2.3B + $19.1B = $21.4B multiplies out. The only strain is the 6.5M branded users against generic step therapy.
rationale.generativity: The prose and world fields imply many scenes and characters: skip-week parties, 'natty' dating profiles, DEXA technicians in BUILT NOT BOUGHT shirts, steakhouse abundance displays, PBM scale programmes, and Discord peptide vendors. The day-in-the-life with Ray shows rather than explains, through the 6:10 scale chime, the butter-drawer pen, the song that does nothing, and the pencilled CAKE against the 80% adherence math.

least_plausible_claims.quote: CMS launches a CMMI model giving $0 generic semaglutide to eligible Medicare and Medicaid enrollees in 24 states
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: the model starts in Jan 2028, but the candidate says licensed generics only reached US pharmacies from Apr 2028, so there was no generic to give away for the first quarter. The 65+ rise from 9% to 12% and the 18% six-month failure cohort are also pinned on a programme that had under a year of generic supply.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Branded drugs (tirzepatide, oral Wegovy, Foundayo) stay at the Nov 2025 deal rate of ~$245/month with a $50 copay, under step therapy.
least_plausible_claims.why: magnitude: the same note says oral Wegovy and Foundayo cash prices fell to $99–149, so Medicare would pay 65–145% more than the cash price. That makes the ~$19.1B branded spending figure inconsistent with the price collapse.

magnitude: 0.9% of all under-18s is roughly 650k children, about 2.5% of adolescents. That is roughly an eightfold jump from the parent's ~0.6% of children with obesity, in two years, with generics available for only part of 2028. No pediatric-specific mechanism is shown.

rationale.badness: Cheap generic access is a real gain, but it is paid for with conditioning. The free tier requires ≥80% refill adherence, monthly cellular-scale weigh-ins and ≥5% loss, and about 18% of enrollees lost $0 status. The conditioning also collides with drug holidays, the standard remedy for the 20–25% reporting flattening. Fracture rates 25–35% higher in users 65+ and a gray market with no oversight add physical harm, and weight data is shared with plan sponsors. Harm is real but nameable and measured, and obesity is still falling, so this is a harder society rather than a refusable one.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visibly realised and traceable to events or fields. The generic settlement, $0 subsidy with conditioning, bone/muscle warning, oral parity via the high-dose label, 503B-driven gray market, natty/muscle inversion, mainstream flattening, and no new indication all appear. Retatrutide (filed Mar 2027, approved Apr 2028) and CagriSema are allowed by the approval rules. mechanism: the chains are mostly shown (settlement → $49 pens → down-market F&B; conditioning → failed checks → gray market). The $0 generic programme starting Jan 2028 before generics shipped in Apr 2028 is a timing contradiction (claim 1), and attributing the 65+ rise to the programme is thin. The pediatric jump is asserted (claim 3). magnitude: headline figures sit inside the envelope (15%, 21%, age bands ≈15.0%, cycling 7.5/21, payer split sums to ~39.8M, $2.3B + $19.1B ≈ $21.4B). The Medicare $245 branded price versus $99–149 cash (claim 2) and the ~5x jump in annual public spend over the parent's CBO scale are unreconciled.
rationale.generativity: The Ray Delgado scene is concrete and specific: the 6:10 scale chime, the thigh injection, the DEXA technician in a BUILT NOT BOUGHT shirt, the song that doesn't land, and the adherence-versus-quinceañera dilemma written as CAKE in pencil. The world fields also imply many more characters and scenes: skip-week parties, natty dating profiles, strip-mall muscle clinics, Discord peptide vendors, couples therapists, and attorneys general contesting weight-data sharing.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot ends and CMS launches a CMMI model giving $0 generic semaglutide to eligible Medicare and Medicaid enrollees in 24 states
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the model starts in Jan 2028 and hands out $0 generic semaglutide, but generics only reach US pharmacies in Apr 2028. The 18% six-month-check failures and 4.5M generic enrollees by Dec 2028 are squeezed into the months after launch.

Mechanism and magnitude: the world says generic substitution and step therapy dominate, yet 6.5M public users (59%) stay on branded drugs at Dec 2028, only nine months after generics arrive. The prose then says the programme 'costs about two billion dollars a year', ignoring the $19B branded line.

Magnitude: 0.9% of all under-18s is about 650k children. The parent had only ~0.6% of children with obesity on the drug, which is roughly 0.1% of all children, so this is a many-fold jump in two years with no pediatric driver or mechanism.

rationale.badness: The world is recognisably harder. Free coverage is conditioned on cellular-scale weigh-ins and ≥80% refill adherence, and about 18% of enrollees lose $0 status at the first check. 65+ users face fracture and sarcopenia risk, 20–25% report flattening, and the offshore gray market has 2.5M exclusive users. Offsets are cheap access, falling obesity, and a flattened thinness gradient, so inequality is mixed. Harms are mostly named and measured, so the epistemic score stays moderate. Overall is a middle-to-hard 5.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visible in fields and events: 15% adoption, a settlement-driven generic collapse, adherence conditioning, the bone/muscle warning, orforglipron parity, gray-market regrowth, the 'natty' inversion, the $0 subsidy, and mainstream flattening. Approvals follow the envelope (CagriSema Jan 2027, retatrutide 13 months after filing). mechanism: causal chains are mostly shown, but the $0 generic model starts in Jan 2028 before generics exist (claim 1), and branded drugs dominate public volume despite generic-first step therapy (claim 2). The flip of the culture toward muscle is partly asserted. magnitude: 15% current and 21% ever are inside the envelope, and the cycling, age-band, payer-split and $2.3B/$19.1B arithmetic all reconcile. Deductions are for the pediatric 0.9% jump (claim 3) and the prose '$2B a year' that contradicts the $21.4B total.
rationale.generativity: The Ray Delgado scene is concrete: the 6:10 scale chime, the butter-drawer pen, the DEXA tech in a BUILT NOT BOUGHT shirt, the unmoved song, and the CAKE pencil mark against the 80% refill threshold. The world also implies many more scenes: skip-week parties, 'natty' dating profiles, PBM weigh-in disputes, and gray-market Discord vendors.
